A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with readable text, equations, nine figures, two tables, and references. All pages were inspected; neither version contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 surveys results attributed to prior work rather than reporting original empirical studies. Its figures are explanatory illustrations; Figure 8(b) explicitly adapts an earlier publication.

after.justification: v2 remains a survey without original empirical results. Newly mentioned numerical verification, correlations, and sparse-training findings are explicitly attributed to cited papers.

M1.justification: Neither version develops a proposed learning algorithm or model. The new LoRA and lightning-attention passages describe existing architectures and their symmetries.

E1.justification: Neither PDF reports datasets or tasks used in evaluations conducted by this work. Newly discussed architectures and applications expand literature coverage, not evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baseline comparisons. Table 2 retains the same catalogue of ENorm, weight balancing, teleportation, and Goldstone-GD methods; additional citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: No experimental splits, training budgets, sample sizes, evaluation metrics, or testing procedures are introduced or revised. The added passages summarize existing research.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness study, sensitivity test, or error analysis is added. The explanatory illustrations remain, while the new examples concern mathematical symmetries rather than experimental analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Newly cited correlation findings do not introduce uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds cited qualitative findings: Henry et al.'s numerical verification of symmetry breaking when restoring softmax, da Silva et al.'s curvature–generalization correlation, and Adnan et al.'s sparse-training result (Sections 2.4, 7.2, and 7.3). These were absent from v1 and are literature summaries, not original experiments.

T1.justification: Example 2.12 adds the explicit LoRA symmetry action (U,V) -> (Ug^-1,gV). Section 2.4 adds cited symmetry and identifiability characterizations for polynomial networks and lightning self-attention. The existing formal framework is retained, without new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are unchanged, and the introduction retains the same contribution: surveying parameter-space symmetry, connecting it to learning theory, and identifying open problems.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 now explicitly cautions that mode connectivity can arise beyond symmetry. Section 7.2 replaces the standalone initialization discussion with an interpretation of symmetry-aware sharpness and generalization. Section 7.3 replaces the emphasis on small image-classification studies with proposed practical barriers to adoption.

D1.justification: No implementation settings, hardware information, training costs, or code/data access instructions are added or revised. The new architecture examples provide mathematical descriptions rather than reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references on LoRA, polynomial and lightning-attention identifiability, quotient-geometry sharpness, and sparse-subnetwork alignment, plus Belkin et al. in the introduction. These extend existing survey themes without changing its overall research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds explanatory transitions, expands the transformer subsection title, condenses Section 5.2, and locally rewrites Section 7. The eight-section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: All nine figures and two tables are retained. Figures 4 and 8 receive visual adjustments; Figure 8 moves from page 16 to 17, and Table 2 from page 13 to 14. These are localized display and placement changes.

improvement.justification: The explicit qualification of symmetry-based mode connectivity improves precision, while the LoRA example and updated identifiability discussion improve explanatory coverage. Replacing speculative initialization discussion with a cited quotient-geometry account strengthens Section 7.2; initialization remains discussed in Section 5.2. These are useful, targeted improvements to an otherwise stable survey.
